AWSTemplateFormatVersion: '2010-09-09'
Description: >
  AWS CloudFormation template to deploy an AWS Backup Audit Manager framework with
  five default compliance controls for backup protection, encryption, deletion protection,
  minimum retention, and backup frequency verification, including prerequisite AWS Config setup
  with a Customer Managed KMS Key (CMK) for S3 bucket encryption.

Parameters:
  FrameworkName:
    Type: String
    Default: BackupComplianceFramework
    Description: Name of the AWS Backup Audit Manager Framework. Must be unique within the account and region.
    AllowedPattern: '^[a-zA-Z][a-zA-Z0-9_]{0,255}$'
    ConstraintDescription: Must start with a letter and contain only alphanumeric characters or underscores, up to 256 characters.

  FrameworkDescription:
    Type: String
    Default: Framework evaluating compliance against default backup policies including retention, frequency, and encryption.
    Description: Description of the AWS Backup Audit Manager Framework.
    MaxLength: 1024

  RequiredRetentionDays:
    Type: Number
    Default: 35
    MinValue: 1
    MaxValue: 36500
    Description: Minimum retention period in days required for recovery points and backup plans.

  RequiredFrequencyValue:
    Type: Number
    Default: 24
    MinValue: 1
    MaxValue: 1000
    Description: Maximum interval allowed between backup executions.

  RequiredFrequencyUnit:
    Type: String
    Default: hours
    AllowedValues:
      - hours
      - days
      - weeks
      - months
    Description: Unit of time for the backup frequency requirement.

Resources:
  # ----------------------------------------------------------------------
  # KMS Key & Alias for AWS Config S3 Bucket Encryption
  # ----------------------------------------------------------------------
  ConfigKmsKey:
    Type: AWS::KMS::Key
    Properties:
      Description: Customer Managed Key for AWS Config S3 bucket encryption
      EnableKeyRotation: true
      KeyPolicy:
        Version: '2012-10-17'
        Id: ConfigKmsKeyPolicy
        Statement:
          - Sid: EnableRootAccess
            Effect: Allow
            Principal:
              AWS: !Sub 'arn:aws:iam::${AWS::AccountId}:root'
            Action: kms:*
            Resource: '*'
          - Sid: AllowAWSConfigKmsUsage
            Effect: Allow
            Principal:
              Service: config.amazonaws.com
            Action:
              - kms:Decrypt
              - kms:GenerateDataKey
              - kms:DescribeKey
            Resource: '*'
            Condition:
              StringEquals:
                aws:SourceAccount: !Ref AWS::AccountId

  ConfigKmsKeyAlias:
    Type: AWS::KMS::Alias
    Properties:
      AliasName: !Sub 'alias/config-bucket-key-${AWS::StackName}'
      TargetKeyId: !Ref ConfigKmsKey

  # ----------------------------------------------------------------------
  # S3 Bucket & Policy for AWS Config
  # ----------------------------------------------------------------------
  ConfigBucket:
    Type: AWS::S3::Bucket
    DeletionPolicy: Retain
    UpdateReplacePolicy: Retain
    Properties:
      BucketEncryption:
        ServerSideEncryptionConfiguration:
          - ServerSideEncryptionByDefault:
              SSEAlgorithm: aws:kms
              KMSMasterKeyID: !GetAtt ConfigKmsKey.Arn
            BucketKeyEnabled: true
      PublicAccessBlockConfiguration:
        BlockPublicAcls: true
        BlockPublicPolicy: true
        IgnorePublicAcls: true
        RestrictPublicBuckets: true

  ConfigBucketPolicy:
    Type: AWS::S3::BucketPolicy
    Properties:
      Bucket: !Ref ConfigBucket
      PolicyDocument:
        Version: '2012-10-17'
        Statement:
          - Sid: AWSConfigBucketPermissionsCheck
            Effect: Allow
            Principal:
              Service: config.amazonaws.com
            Action: s3:GetBucketAcl
            Resource: !GetAtt ConfigBucket.Arn
            Condition:
              StringEquals:
                aws:SourceAccount: !Ref AWS::AccountId
          - Sid: AWSConfigBucketExistenceCheck
            Effect: Allow
            Principal:
              Service: config.amazonaws.com
            Action: s3:ListBucket
            Resource: !GetAtt ConfigBucket.Arn
            Condition:
              StringEquals:
                aws:SourceAccount: !Ref AWS::AccountId
          - Sid: AWSConfigBucketDelivery
            Effect: Allow
            Principal:
              Service: config.amazonaws.com
            Action: s3:PutObject
            Resource: !Sub '${ConfigBucket.Arn}/AWSLogs/${AWS::AccountId}/Config/*'
            Condition:
              StringEquals:
                s3:x-amz-acl: bucket-owner-full-control
                aws:SourceAccount: !Ref AWS::AccountId

  # ----------------------------------------------------------------------
  # IAM Role for AWS Config
  # ----------------------------------------------------------------------
  ConfigRole:
    Type: AWS::IAM::Role
    Properties:
      RoleName: !Sub 'aws-config-role-${AWS::Region}-${AWS::StackName}'
      AssumeRolePolicyDocument:
        Version: '2012-10-17'
        Statement:
          - Effect: Allow
            Principal:
              Service: config.amazonaws.com
            Action: sts:AssumeRole
      ManagedPolicyArns:
        - arn:aws:iam::aws:policy/service-role/AWS_ConfigRole

  # ----------------------------------------------------------------------
  # AWS Config Recorder & Delivery Channel
  # ----------------------------------------------------------------------
  ConfigRecorder:
    Type: AWS::Config::ConfigurationRecorder
    Properties:
      Name: default
      RoleARN: !GetAtt ConfigRole.Arn
      RecordingGroup:
        AllSupported: true
        IncludeGlobalResourceTypes: true

  ConfigDeliveryChannel:
    Type: AWS::Config::DeliveryChannel
    DependsOn: ConfigBucketPolicy
    Properties:
      Name: default
      S3BucketName: !Ref ConfigBucket

  # ----------------------------------------------------------------------
  # AWS Backup Audit Manager Framework
  # ----------------------------------------------------------------------
  BackupAuditFramework:
    Type: AWS::Backup::Framework
    DependsOn:
      - ConfigRecorder
      - ConfigDeliveryChannel
    Properties:
      FrameworkName: !Ref FrameworkName
      FrameworkDescription: !Ref FrameworkDescription
      FrameworkControls:
        - ControlName: BACKUP_RESOURCES_PROTECTED_BY_BACKUP_PLAN

        - ControlName: BACKUP_RECOVERY_POINT_ENCRYPTED

        - ControlName: BACKUP_RECOVERY_POINT_MANUAL_DELETION_DISABLED

        - ControlName: BACKUP_RECOVERY_POINT_MINIMUM_RETENTION_CHECK
          ControlInputParameters:
            - ParameterName: requiredRetentionDays
              ParameterValue: !Sub '${RequiredRetentionDays}'

        - ControlName: BACKUP_PLAN_MIN_FREQUENCY_AND_MIN_RETENTION_CHECK
          ControlInputParameters:
            - ParameterName: requiredFrequencyValue
              ParameterValue: !Sub '${RequiredFrequencyValue}'
            - ParameterName: requiredFrequencyUnit
              ParameterValue: !Ref RequiredFrequencyUnit
            - ParameterName: requiredRetentionDays
              ParameterValue: !Sub '${RequiredRetentionDays}'

      FrameworkTags:
        - Key: ManagedBy
          Value: CloudFormation
        - Key: Purpose
          Value: BackupAuditManagerCompliance

Outputs:
  FrameworkArn:
    Description: The Amazon Resource Name (ARN) of the AWS Backup Audit Manager Framework.
    Value: !GetAtt BackupAuditFramework.FrameworkArn

  FrameworkName:
    Description: The name of the AWS Backup Audit Manager Framework.

    Value: !Ref ConfigBucket

  ConfigKmsKeyArn:
    Description: KMS Key ARN used for encrypting AWS Config S3 bucket.
    Value: !GetAtt ConfigKmsKey.Arn

AWSTemplateFormatVersion: "2010-09-09"
Description: Serverless workflow that publishes custom events to a custom EventBridge bus and forwards all events to a CloudWatch Logs log group.

Parameters:
  EventBusName:
    Type: String
    Default: CustomEventBus
    Description: Name of the custom EventBridge event bus.
  LogGroupName:
    Type: String
    Default: /aws/events/custom-event-bus
    Description: Name of the CloudWatch Logs log group that receives all forwarded events.

Resources:
  # Custom EventBridge event bus that receives custom events.
  CustomEventBus:
    Type: AWS::Events::EventBus
    Properties:
      Name: !Ref EventBusName

  # CloudWatch Logs log group used for testing and debugging.
  CustomLogGroup:
    Type: AWS::Logs::LogGroup
    Properties:
      LogGroupName: !Ref LogGroupName
      RetentionInDays: 14

  # Resource-based policy granting EventBridge permission to write to the log group.
  EventBusToLogGroupPolicy:
    Type: AWS::Logs::ResourcePolicy
    Properties:
      PolicyName: EventsToCustomLogGroup
      PolicyDocument: !Sub |
        {
          "Version": "2012-10-17",
          "Statement": [
            {
              "Effect": "Allow",
              "Principal": {
                "Service": "events.amazonaws.com"
              },
              "Action": [
                "logs:CreateLogStream",
                "logs:PutLogEvents"
              ],
              "Resource": "arn:aws:logs:${AWS::Region}:${AWS::AccountId}:log-group:${CustomLogGroup}:*"
            }
          ]
        }

  # Rule that forwards all events arriving on the custom bus to the log group.
  ForwardAllEventsRule:
    Type: AWS::Events::Rule
    Properties:
      EventBusName: !Ref CustomEventBus
      Name: !Sub "forward-all-${EventBusName}-to-logs"
      EventPattern:
        source:
          - prefix: ""
      State: ENABLED
      Targets:
        - Arn: !GetAtt CustomLogGroup.Arn
          Id: "CustomLogGroupTarget"

  # IAM role assumed by Step Functions to publish events to the custom bus.
  StateMachineRole:
    Type: AWS::IAM::Role
    Properties:
      AssumeRolePolicyDocument:
        Version: "2012-10-17"
        Statement:
          - Effect: Allow
            Principal:
              Service: states.amazonaws.com
            Action: sts:AssumeRole
      Policies:
        - PolicyName: PublishEventsPolicy
          PolicyDocument:
            Version: "2012-10-17"
            Statement:
              - Effect: Allow
                Action:
                  - events:PutEvents
                Resource: !GetAtt CustomEventBus.Arn

  # Serverless workflow (Step Functions state machine) that sends a custom event.
  StateMachine:
    Type: AWS::StepFunctions::StateMachine
    Properties:
      StateMachineName: !Sub "custom-event-publisher"
      RoleArn: !GetAtt StateMachineRole.Arn
      DefinitionString: !Sub |
        {
          "Comment": "Serverless workflow that publishes a custom event to the custom EventBridge bus",
          "StartAt": "PublishCustomEvent",
          "States": {
            "PublishCustomEvent": {
              "Type": "Task",
              "Resource": "arn:aws:states:::aws-sdk:eventbridge:putEvents",
              "Parameters": {
                "Entries": [
                  {
                    "EventBusName": "${CustomEventBus}",
                    "Source": "custom.workflow.source",
                    "DetailType": "CustomWorkflowEvent",
                    "Detail": "{\"message\": \"Hello from the serverless workflow\", \"runId\":\"${!AWS::Execution.Id}\"}"
                  }
                ]
              },
              "End": true
            }
          }
        }

Outputs:
  StateMachineArn:
    Description: ARN of the Step Functions state machine.
    Value: !Ref StateMachine
  CustomEventBusArn:
    Description: ARN of the custom EventBridge event bus.
    Value: !GetAtt CustomEventBus.Arn
  LogGroupArn:
    Description: ARN of the CloudWatch Logs log group.
    Value: !GetAtt CustomLogGroup.Arn
  RuleArn:
    Description: ARN of the CloudWatch Events forwarding rule.
    Value: !GetAtt ForwardAllEventsRule.Arn

final_template:
AWSTemplateFormatVersion: 2010-09-09
Description: >-
  WAF WebACL for a CloudFront distribution protecting a Spree Commerce
  application. Combines AWS managed rule groups for common web threats, known
  bad inputs, SQL injection and Linux exploits (the first three scoped away
  from /admin paths), adds a per-IP rate limit and blocks bot user agents while
  allowing legitimate crawlers (Googlebot, Bingbot).

Parameters:
  EnvironmentName:
    Type: String
    Default: spree-production
    Description: Name of the environment used to prefix resource names.
  RateLimit:
    Type: Number
    Default: 2000
    MinValue: 100
    MaxValue: 2000000
    Description: Maximum number of requests per 5-minute period from a single IP address.

Conditions:
  # CloudFront WAF WebACLs must be deployed in us-east-1.
  IsUsEast1: !Equals [!Ref "AWS::Region", "us-east-1"]

Resources:
  # --------------------------------------------------------------------------
  # Origin for the CloudFront distribution (private S3 bucket using OAI)
  # --------------------------------------------------------------------------
  SpreeOriginBucket:
    Type: AWS::S3::Bucket
    Condition: IsUsEast1
    Properties:
      BucketEncryption:
        ServerSideEncryptionConfiguration:
          - ServerSideEncryptionByDefault:
              KMSMasterKeyID: !Ref SpreeBucketKMSKey
              SSEAlgorithm: aws:kms
      PublicAccessBlockConfiguration:
        BlockPublicAcls: true
        BlockPublicPolicy: true
        IgnorePublicAcls: true
        RestrictPublicBuckets: true
      VersioningConfiguration:
        Status: Enabled

  SpreeBucketKMSKey:
    Type: AWS::KMS::Key
    Condition: IsUsEast1
    Properties:
      Description: !Sub "KMS key for encrypting the ${EnvironmentName} Spree Commerce origin bucket"
      EnableKeyRotation: true
      KeyPolicy:
        Version: "2012-10-17"
        Statement:
          - Sid: EnableIAM
            Effect: Allow
            Principal:
              AWS: !Sub "arn:${AWS::Partition}:iam::${AWS::AccountId}:root"
            Action: kms:*
            Resource: "*"

  SpreeBucketKMSKeyAlias:
    Type: AWS::KMS::Alias
    Condition: IsUsEast1
    Properties:
      AliasName: !Sub "alias/${EnvironmentName}-spree-bucket-key"
      TargetKeyId: !Ref SpreeBucketKMSKey

  OriginAccessIdentity:
    Type: AWS::CloudFront::CloudFrontOriginAccessIdentity
    Condition: IsUsEast1
    Properties:
      CloudFrontOriginAccessIdentityConfig:
        Comment: !Sub "Origin access identity for the ${EnvironmentName} Spree Commerce distribution"

  SpreeOriginBucketPolicy:
    Type: AWS::S3::BucketPolicy
    Condition: IsUsEast1
    Properties:
      Bucket: !Ref SpreeOriginBucket
      PolicyDocument:
        Version: "2012-10-17"
        Statement:
          - Sid: AllowCloudFrontRead
            Effect: Allow
            Principal:
              CanonicalUser: !GetAtt OriginAccessIdentity.S3CanonicalUserId
            Action: s3:GetObject
            Resource: !Sub "${SpreeOriginBucket.Arn}/*"

  CloudFrontDistribution:
    Type: AWS::CloudFront::Distribution
    Condition: IsUsEast1
    Properties:
      DistributionConfig:
        Enabled: true
        HttpVersion: http2
        DefaultRootObject: index.html
        PriceClass: PriceClass_100
        Comment: !Sub "CloudFront distribution for the ${EnvironmentName} Spree Commerce application"
        WebACLId: !GetAtt WAFWebACL.Arn
        ViewerCertificate:
          CloudFrontDefaultCertificate: true
          MinimumProtocolVersion: TLSv1.2_2021
        Origins:
          - Id: SpreeOrigin
            DomainName: !GetAtt SpreeOriginBucket.RegionalDomainName
            S3OriginConfig:
              OriginAccessIdentity: !Sub "origin-access-identity/cloudfront/${OriginAccessIdentity}"
        DefaultCacheBehavior:
          TargetOriginId: SpreeOrigin
          ViewerProtocolPolicy: redirect-to-https
          Compress: true
          AllowedMethods:
            - GET
            - HEAD
            - OPTIONS
          CachedMethods:
            - GET
            - HEAD
          ForwardedValues:
            QueryString: true
            Cookies:
              Forward: all

  # --------------------------------------------------------------------------
  # WAF WebACL (CLOUDFRONT scope)
  # --------------------------------------------------------------------------
  WAFWebACL:
    Type: AWS::WAFv2::WebACL
    Condition: IsUsEast1
    Properties:
      Name: !Sub "${EnvironmentName}-waf-webacl"
      Scope: CLOUDFRONT
      Description: !Sub "WAF WebACL protecting the ${EnvironmentName} Spree Commerce CloudFront distribution."
      DefaultAction:
        Allow: {}
      CustomResponseBodies:
        RateLimitResponse:
          ContentType: TEXT_PLAIN
          Content: '{"error": "rate limit exceeded"}'
      VisibilityConfig:
        SampledRequestsEnabled: true
        CloudWatchMetricsEnabled: true
        MetricName: !Sub "${EnvironmentName}-waf-webacl"
      Rules:
        # AWS managed rule group: common web threats, excluding /admin paths.
        - Name: AWSManagedRulesCommonRuleSet
          Priority: 1
          OverrideAction:
            None: {}
          VisibilityConfig:
            SampledRequestsEnabled: true
            CloudWatchMetricsEnabled: true
            MetricName: !Sub "${EnvironmentName}-common-rule-set"
          Statement:
            ManagedRuleGroupStatement:
              VendorName: AWS
              Name: AWSManagedRulesCommonRuleSet
              ScopeDownStatement:
                NotStatement:
                  Statement:
                    ByteMatchStatement:
                      FieldToMatch:
                        UriPath: {}
                      PositionalConstraint: STARTS_WITH
                      SearchString: /admin
                      TextTransformations:
                        - Priority: 0
                          Type: NONE

        # AWS managed rule group: known bad inputs, excluding /admin paths.
        - Name: AWSManagedRulesKnownBadInputsRuleSet
          Priority: 2
          OverrideAction:
            None: {}
          VisibilityConfig:
            SampledRequestsEnabled: true
            CloudWatchMetricsEnabled: true
            MetricName: !Sub "${EnvironmentName}-known-bad-inputs-rule-set"
          Statement:
            ManagedRuleGroupStatement:
              VendorName: AWS
              Name: AWSManagedRulesKnownBadInputsRuleSet
              ScopeDownStatement:
                NotStatement:
                  Statement:
                    ByteMatchStatement:
                      FieldToMatch:
                        UriPath: {}
                      PositionalConstraint: STARTS_WITH
                      SearchString: /admin
                      TextTransformations:
                        - Priority: 0
                          Type: NONE

        # AWS managed rule group: SQL injection, excluding /admin paths.
        - Name: AWSManagedRulesSQLiRuleSet
          Priority: 3
          OverrideAction:
            None: {}
          VisibilityConfig:
            SampledRequestsEnabled: true
            CloudWatchMetricsEnabled: true
            MetricName: !Sub "${EnvironmentName}-sqli-rule-set"
          Statement:
            ManagedRuleGroupStatement:
              VendorName: AWS
              Name: AWSManagedRulesSQLiRuleSet
              ScopeDownStatement:
                NotStatement:
                  Statement:
                    ByteMatchStatement:
                      FieldToMatch:
                        UriPath: {}
                      PositionalConstraint: STARTS_WITH
                      SearchString: /admin
                      TextTransformations:
                        - Priority: 0
                          Type: NONE

        # AWS managed rule group: Linux exploits (applies to all paths).
        - Name: AWSManagedRulesLinuxRuleSet
          Priority: 4
          OverrideAction:
            None: {}
          VisibilityConfig:
            SampledRequestsEnabled: true
            CloudWatchMetricsEnabled: true
            MetricName: !Sub "${EnvironmentName}-linux-rule-set"
          Statement:
            ManagedRuleGroupStatement:
              VendorName: AWS
              Name: AWSManagedRulesLinuxRuleSet

        # Rate limiting: max RateLimit requests per 5-minute window per IP.
        - Name: RateLimit
          Priority: 5
          Action:
            Block:
              CustomResponse:
                ResponseCode: 429
                CustomResponseBodyKey: RateLimitResponse
          VisibilityConfig:
            SampledRequestsEnabled: true
            CloudWatchMetricsEnabled: true
            MetricName: !Sub "${EnvironmentName}-rate-limit"
          Statement:
            RateBasedStatement:
              Limit: !Ref RateLimit
              AggregateKeyType: IP

        # Block generic bots while allowing legitimate crawlers.
        - Name: BlockBotUserAgents
          Priority: 6
          Action:
            Block:
              CustomResponse:
                ResponseCode: 403
          VisibilityConfig:
            SampledRequestsEnabled: true
            CloudWatchMetricsEnabled: true
            MetricName: !Sub "${EnvironmentName}-block-bot-user-agents"
          Statement:
            AndStatement:
              Statements:
                - ByteMatchStatement:
                    FieldToMatch:
                      SingleHeader:
                        Name: user-agent
                    PositionalConstraint: CONTAINS
                    SearchString: bot
                    TextTransformations:
                      - Priority: 0
                        Type: NONE
                - NotStatement:
                    Statement:
                      OrStatement:
                        Statements:
                          - ByteMatchStatement:
                              FieldToMatch:
                                SingleHeader:
                                  Name: user-agent
                              PositionalConstraint: CONTAINS
                              SearchString: Googlebot
                              TextTransformations:
                                - Priority: 0
                                  Type: NONE
                          - ByteMatchStatement:
                              FieldToMatch:
                                SingleHeader:
                                  Name: user-agent
                              PositionalConstraint: CONTAINS
                              SearchString: Bingbot
                              TextTransformations:
                                - Priority: 0
                                  Type: NONE

Outputs:
  WAFWebACLArn:
    Condition: IsUsEast1
    Description: ARN of the WAF WebACL.

Description: >-

  Step Functions state machine when an instance transitions to running, stopped,

        bus targeting running, stopped, and terminated states.
      EventBusName: default
      EventPattern:
        source:
          - aws.ec2
        detail-type:
          - EC2 Instance State-change Notification
        detail:
          state:
            - running
            - stopped
            - terminated
      State: ENABLED
      Targets:
        - Arn: !GetAtt EC2StateMachine.Arn
          Id: StepFunctionsTarget
          RoleArn: !GetAtt EventsToStepFunctionsRole.Arn

  # Role that allows EventBridge to start state machine executions
  EventsToStepFunctionsRole:
    Type: AWS::IAM::Role
    Properties:
      AssumeRolePolicyDocument:
        Version: "2012-10-17"
        Statement:
          - Effect: Allow
            Principal:

              "Type": "Choice",

      Description: KMS key for encrypting CloudTrail S3 bucket

      KeyPolicy:
        Version: "2012-10-17"
        Statement:
          - Sid: Enable IAM User Permissions
            Effect: Allow
            Principal:
              AWS: !Sub "arn:aws:iam::${AWS::AccountId}:root"
            Action: kms:*
            Resource: "*"

  BucketEncryptionKeyAlias:
    Type: AWS::KMS::Alias
    Properties:
      AliasName: !Sub "alias/${AWS::StackName}-log-bucket"
      TargetKeyId: !Ref BucketEncryptionKey

  GlueDatabase:
    Type: AWS::Glue::Database
    Properties:
      CatalogId: !Ref AWS::AccountId
      DatabaseInput:
        Name: !Sub "${AWS::StackName}-kk-admin-db"
        Description: Database for querying CloudTrail logs with Athena.

  GlueCrawlerRole:

      AssumeRolePolicyDocument:

                  - s3:ListBucket

              - Effect: Allow

AWSTemplateFormatVersion: "2010-09-09"

Description: >-
  Creates foundational infrastructure for Amazon ECS Anywhere: an ECS cluster,
  an IAM role that grants the permissions required to register and manage
  external (on-premises and edge) container instances, and an AWS Systems
  Manager (SSM) Command document used during the external instance registration
  process.

Parameters:
  ClusterName:
    Type: String
    Description: Name to assign to the ECS Anywhere cluster.
    Default: ecs-anywhere-cluster

Resources:
  # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
  # ECS cluster that external container instances register with.
  # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
  ECSAnywhereCluster:
    Type: AWS::ECS::Cluster
    Properties:
      ClusterName: !Ref ClusterName

  # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
  # IAM role used by external container instances (ECS Agent + SSM Agent).
  # The SSM Agent assumes this role after a hybrid instance registration, and
  # the ECS Agent uses it to register the instance with the cluster, report
  # state, and pull container images.
  # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
  ECSAnywhereInstanceRole:
    Type: AWS::IAM::Role
    Properties:
      RoleName: ecs-anywhere-instance-role
      Path: /
      AssumeRolePolicyDocument:
        Version: "2012-10-17"
        Statement:
          - Effect: Allow
            Principal:
              Service: ssm.amazonaws.com
            Action: sts:AssumeRole
      ManagedPolicyArns:
        # Lets the ECS Agent register the external instance, submit state, and
        # pull images from Amazon ECR.
        - arn:aws:iam::aws:policy/service-role/AmazonEC2ContainerServiceforEC2Role
        # Lets the SSM Agent create and use a hybrid activation and the managed
        # instance registration flow.
        - arn:aws:iam::aws:policy/AmazonSSMManagedInstanceCore
      Policies:
        - PolicyName: ECSAnywhereActivationManagement
          PolicyDocument:
            Version: "2012-10-17"
            Statement:
              - Sid: ManageHybridActivations
                Effect: Allow
                Action:
                  - ssm:CreateActivation
                  - ssm:DescribeActivations
                  - ssm:DeleteActivation
                  - ssm:DescribeInstanceInformation
                  - ssm:DeregisterManagedInstance
                Resource: "*"

  # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
  # SSM Command document used by the registration process. It references the
  # target cluster and accepts a configurable external instance name, configures
  # the ECS Agent for an external instance, and registers the host with SSM.
  # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
  SSMRegistrationDocument:
    Type: AWS::SSM::Document
    Properties:
      Name: ecs-anywhere-register
      DocumentType: Command
      Content:
        schemaVersion: "2.2"
        description: >-
          Registers and manages an ECS Anywhere external container instance and
          associates it with the target ECS cluster.
        parameters:
          ECSCluster:
            type: String
            default: !Ref ClusterName
            description: >-
              (Required) Name of the ECS Anywhere cluster to register the
              external container instance with.
          ContainerInstanceName:
            type: String
            description: >-
              (Required) A unique, configurable name to assign to the external
              container instance.
          SSMActivationId:
            type: String
            description: >-
              (Required) SSM activation ID used to register the hybrid
              (managed) instance.
          SSMActivationCode:
            type: String
            description: >-
              (Required) SSM activation code used to register the hybrid
              (managed) instance.
        mainSteps:
          - action: aws:runShellScript
            name: registerEcsAnywhereInstance
            inputs:
              timeoutSeconds: "600"
              runCommand:
                - |
                  #!/bin/bash
                  set -euo pipefail

                  ECS_CLUSTER='{{ ECSCluster }}'
                  INSTANCE_NAME='{{ ContainerInstanceName }}'
                  ACTIVATION_ID='{{ SSMActivationId }}'
                  ACTIVATION_CODE='{{ SSMActivationCode }}'

                  # Configure the ECS Agent as an external (ECS Anywhere)
                  # instance pointing at the target cluster.
                  sudo mkdir -p /etc/ecs
                  sudo tee /etc/ecs/ecs.config > /dev/null <<EOF
                  ECS_CLUSTER=${ECS_CLUSTER}
                  ECS_EXTERNAL=true
                  ECS_AVOID_DUPLICATE_IP=true
                  EOF

                  # Register/configures this host as a hybrid managed instance
                  # with SSM using the provided activation, if not yet done.
                  if [ ! -d /var/lib/amazon/ssm/i-* ] 2>/dev/null; then
                    sudo amazon-ssm-agent-registration \
                      --activation-id "${ACTIVATION_ID}" \
                      --activation-code "${ACTIVATION_CODE}" \
                      --instance-name "${INSTANCE_NAME}" || true
                  fi

                  # Ensure the SSM Agent is running so the instance stays
                  # connected to the ECS Anywhere control plane.
                  sudo systemctl enable --now amazon-ssm-agent 2>/dev/null || true
      Tags:
        - Key: Purpose
          Value: ECS-Anywhere

Outputs:
  ClusterName:
    Description: Name of the ECS Anywhere cluster.
    Value: !Ref ECSAnywhereCluster
  ClusterArn:
    Description: ARN of the ECS Anywhere cluster.
    Value: !GetAtt ECSAnywhereCluster.Arn
  InstanceRoleArn:
    Description: ARN of the IAM role used by external container instances.
    Value: !GetAtt ECSAnywhereInstanceRole.Arn
  SSMRegistrationDocumentName:
    Description: Name of the SSM Command document used for registration.
    Value: !Ref SSMRegistrationDocument

Description: Core event-driven architecture components for a retail demo store application.

Resources:
  # Custom event bus for the retail demo store
  EventBus:
    Type: AWS::Events::EventBus
    Properties:
      Name: retaildemostore-bus

  # CloudWatch log group that receives all events from the catch-all rule
  LogGroup:
    Type: AWS::Logs::LogGroup
    Properties:
      LogGroupName: retaildemostore-bus
      RetentionInDays: 120

  # Resource policy granting EventBridge permission to write events to the log group
  LogGroupPolicy:
    Type: AWS::Logs::ResourcePolicy
    Properties:
      PolicyName: RetailDemoStoreLogDeliveryPolicy
      PolicyDocument:
        Fn::Sub: |-
          {
            "Version": "2012-10-17",
            "Statement": [
              {
                "Effect": "Allow",
                "Principal": {
                  "Service": "events.amazonaws.com"
                },
                "Action": "logs:PutLogEvents",
                "Resource": "arn:aws:logs:${AWS::Region}:${AWS::AccountId}:log-group:${LogGroup}:*"
              }
            ]
          }

  # Disabled catch-all rule that sends all events to the CloudWatch log group
  CatchAllRule:
    Type: AWS::Events::Rule
    Properties:
      Name: retaildemostore-catchall-rule
      EventBusName: !Ref EventBus
      EventPattern: {}
      State: DISABLED
      Targets:
        - Arn: !Sub 'arn:aws:logs:${AWS::Region}:${AWS::AccountId}:log-group:${LogGroup}:*'
          Id: RetailDemoStoreLogTarget

  # Event archive retaining all events on the bus for 120 days
  EventArchive:
    Type: AWS::Events::EventArchive
    Properties:
      ArchiveName: retaildemostore-archive
      EventSourceArn: !GetAtt EventBus.Arn
      RetentionDays: 120

  # Schema discoverer for the event bus
  SchemaDiscoverer:
    Type: AWS::Events::SchemaDiscoverer
    Properties:
      DiscovererName: retaildemostore-discoverer
      SourceArn: !GetAtt EventBus.Arn
      Description: Schema discoverer for the retail demo store event bus

  # SSM parameter storing the event bus name for downstream services
  EventBusSSMParameter:
    Type: AWS::SSM::Parameter
    Properties:
      Type: String
      Name: RetailDemoStore-eventbus
      Value: !Select [1, !Split ['/', !GetAtt EventBus.Arn]]

Outputs:
  EventBusName:
    Description: Name of the retail demo store event bus
    Value: !Select [1, !Split ['/', !GetAtt EventBus.Arn]]
    Export:
      Name: retaildemostore-bus

AWSTemplateFormatVersion: '2010-09-09'
Description: >
  Creates a DynamoDB-based idempotency store for hybrid-mode deduplication,
  where both polling and event-driven workflows may trigger duplicate
  executions on the same file. The table uses a composite primary key, enables
  Time-to-Live with a configurable default of 7 days, enables Point-in-Time
  Recovery by default, and ships a managed IAM policy granting Lambda and
  Step Functions read/write access.

Parameters:
  ProjectPrefix:
    Type: String
    Default: fsxn-s3ap
    Description: Prefix used for naming all resources created by this template.

  TTLDays:
    Type: Number
    Default: 7
    MinValue: 1
    Description: >
      Default number of days after which expired entries are purged from the
      table by DynamoDB Time-to-Live. Applications should record the computed
      expiry timestamp in the TTL attribute.

  TTLAttributeName:
    Type: String
    Default: expiresAt
    Description: >
      Name of the numeric attribute used by DynamoDB Time-to-Live and the
      corresponding attribute defined on the table.

  PITREnabled:
    Type: String
    Default: 'true'
    AllowedValues:
      - 'true'
      - 'false'
    Description: Whether Point-in-Time Recovery is enabled on the table (default true).

Conditions:
  EnablePITR:
    Fn::Equals:
      - !Ref PITREnabled
      - 'true'

Resources:
  IdempotencyTable:
    Type: AWS::DynamoDB::Table
    Properties:
      BillingMode: PAY_PER_REQUEST
      AttributeDefinitions:
        - AttributeName: idempotencyKey
          AttributeType: S
        - AttributeName: scope
          AttributeType: S
      KeySchema:
        - AttributeName: idempotencyKey

                        "S.$": "$.id"

final_template:
AWSTemplateFormatVersion: '2010-09-09'
Description: >
  Chaos engineering workflow that tests the resilience of an ECS service. A
  Step Functions state machine terminates a target EC2 instance, waits 300
  seconds, then checks the health of an ECS service and publishes an SNS alert
  when the service is unhealthy. The template creates all supporting resources:
  VPC networking, an EC2 instance, an ECS cluster/service, an SNS topic, two
  Lambda functions and their IAM roles.

Parameters:
  LatestAmiId:
    Type: AWS::SSM::Parameter::Value<AWS::EC2::Image::Id>
    Default: /aws/service/ami-amazon-linux-latest/al2023-ami-kernel-default-x86_64
    Description: Public SSM parameter path resolving to the latest Amazon Linux 2023 AMI.

Resources:
  ############################################################################
  # Networking
  ############################################################################
  ChaosVpc:
    Type: AWS::EC2::VPC
    Properties:
      CidrBlock: 10.0.0.0/16
      EnableDnsSupport: true
      EnableDnsHostnames: true
      Tags:
        - Key: Name
          Value: chaos-vpc

  ChaosInternetGateway:
    Type: AWS::EC2::InternetGateway
    Properties:
      Tags:
        - Key: Name
          Value: chaos-igw

  ChaosVpcGatewayAttachment:
    Type: AWS::EC2::VPCGatewayAttachment
    Properties:
      VpcId: !Ref ChaosVpc
      InternetGatewayId: !Ref ChaosInternetGateway

  PublicSubnet1:
    Type: AWS::EC2::Subnet
    Properties:
      VpcId: !Ref ChaosVpc
      CidrBlock: 10.0.0.0/24
      AvailabilityZone: !Select [0, !GetAZs '']
      MapPublicIpOnLaunch: false
      Tags:
        - Key: Name
          Value: chaos-public-subnet-1

  PublicSubnet2:
    Type: AWS::EC2::Subnet
    Properties:
      VpcId: !Ref ChaosVpc
      CidrBlock: 10.0.1.0/24
      AvailabilityZone: !Select [1, !GetAZs '']
      MapPublicIpOnLaunch: false
      Tags:
        - Key: Name
          Value: chaos-public-subnet-2

  PublicRouteTable:
    Type: AWS::EC2::RouteTable
    Properties:
      VpcId: !Ref ChaosVpc
      Tags:
        - Key: Name
          Value: chaos-public-rt

  PublicDefaultRoute:
    Type: AWS::EC2::Route
    DependsOn: ChaosVpcGatewayAttachment
    Properties:
      RouteTableId: !Ref PublicRouteTable
      DestinationCidrBlock: 0.0.0.0/0
      GatewayId: !Ref ChaosInternetGateway

  PublicSubnet1RouteTableAssociation:
    Type: AWS::EC2::SubnetRouteTableAssociation
    Properties:
      SubnetId: !Ref PublicSubnet1
      RouteTableId: !Ref PublicRouteTable

  PublicSubnet2RouteTableAssociation:
    Type: AWS::EC2::SubnetRouteTableAssociation
    Properties:
      SubnetId: !Ref PublicSubnet2
      RouteTableId: !Ref PublicRouteTable

  ############################################################################
  # Security groups
  ############################################################################
  Ec2SecurityGroup:
    Type: AWS::EC2::SecurityGroup
    Properties:
      GroupDescription: Security group for the chaos target EC2 instance
      VpcId: !Ref ChaosVpc
      SecurityGroupIngress:
        - IpProtocol: tcp
          FromPort: 22
          ToPort: 22
          CidrIp: 10.0.0.0/16
          Description: SSH from within the VPC only
      Tags:
        - Key: Name
          Value: chaos-ec2-sg

  EcsSecurityGroup:
    Type: AWS::EC2::SecurityGroup
    Properties:
      GroupDescription: Security group for the ECS service tasks
      VpcId: !Ref ChaosVpc
      SecurityGroupIngress:
        - IpProtocol: tcp
          FromPort: 80
          ToPort: 80
          CidrIp: 10.0.0.0/16
          Description: HTTP from within the VPC only
      Tags:
        - Key: Name
          Value: chaos-ecs-sg

  ############################################################################
  # Target EC2 instance that the chaos workflow terminates
  ############################################################################
  ChaosInstance:
    Type: AWS::EC2::Instance
    Properties:
      ImageId: !Ref LatestAmiId
      InstanceType: t3.micro
      Monitoring: true
      SubnetId: !Ref PublicSubnet1
      SecurityGroupIds:
        - !Ref Ec2SecurityGroup
      MetadataOptions:
        HttpEndpoint: enabled
        HttpTokens: required
      BlockDeviceMappings:
        - DeviceName: /dev/xvda
          Ebs:
            VolumeSize: 8
            VolumeType: gp3
            Encrypted: true
      Tags:
        - Key: Name
          Value: chaos-target-instance

  ############################################################################
  # ECS cluster, task definition and service under test
  ############################################################################
  EcsCluster:
    Type: AWS::ECS::Cluster
    Properties:
      ClusterName: chaos-ecs-cluster
      ClusterSettings:
        - Name: containerInsights
          Value: enabled

  EcsLogGroup:
    Type: AWS::Logs::LogGroup
    Properties:
      LogGroupName: /ecs/chaos-task
      RetentionInDays: 30

  EcsTaskExecutionRole:
    Type: AWS::IAM::Role
    Properties:
      AssumeRolePolicyDocument:
        Version: '2012-10-17'
        Statement:
          - Effect: Allow
            Principal:
              Service: ecs-tasks.amazonaws.com
            Action: sts:AssumeRole
      ManagedPolicyArns:
        - !Sub 'arn:${AWS::Partition}:iam::aws:policy/service-role/AmazonECSTaskExecutionRolePolicy'

  EcsTaskDefinition:
    Type: AWS::ECS::TaskDefinition
    Properties:
      Family: chaos-task
      Cpu: '256'
      Memory: '512'
      NetworkMode: awsvpc
      RequiresCompatibilities:
        - FARGATE
      ExecutionRoleArn: !GetAtt EcsTaskExecutionRole.Arn
      ContainerDefinitions:
        - Name: chaos-container
          Image: public.ecr.aws/nginx/nginx:1.25-alpine
          Essential: true
          Privileged: false
          ReadonlyRootFilesystem: true
          User: '101'
          PortMappings:
            - ContainerPort: 80
              Protocol: tcp
          LogConfiguration:
            LogDriver: awslogs
            Options:
              awslogs-group: !Ref EcsLogGroup
              awslogs-region: !Ref AWS::Region
              awslogs-stream-prefix: ecs

  EcsService:
    Type: AWS::ECS::Service
    Properties:
      Cluster: !Ref EcsCluster
      ServiceName: chaos-ecs-service
      TaskDefinition: !Ref EcsTaskDefinition
      DesiredCount: 1
      LaunchType: FARGATE
      NetworkConfiguration:
        AwsvpcConfiguration:
          AssignPublicIp: ENABLED
          SecurityGroups:
            - !Ref EcsSecurityGroup
          Subnets:
            - !Ref PublicSubnet1
            - !Ref PublicSubnet2

  ############################################################################
  # SNS topic (encrypted with a customer managed key) for health alerts
  ############################################################################
  SnsKey:
    Type: AWS::KMS::Key
    Properties:
      Description: KMS key used to encrypt the chaos engineering alert topic
      EnableKeyRotation: true
      KeyPolicy:
        Version: '2012-10-17'
        Statement:
          - Sid: EnableRootPermissions
            Effect: Allow
            Principal:
              AWS: !Sub 'arn:${AWS::Partition}:iam::${AWS::AccountId}:root'
            Action: 'kms:*'
            Resource: '*'

  SnsKeyAlias:
    Type: AWS::KMS::Alias
    Properties:
      AliasName: alias/chaos-alerts
      TargetKeyId: !Ref SnsKey

  ChaosTopic:
    Type: AWS::SNS::Topic
    Properties:
      TopicName: chaos-alerts
      KmsMasterKeyId: !Ref SnsKey

  ############################################################################
  # Lambda permissions
  ############################################################################
  TerminateInstanceRole:
    Type: AWS::IAM::Role
    Properties:
      AssumeRolePolicyDocument:
        Version: '2012-10-17'
        Statement:
          - Effect: Allow
            Principal:
              Service: lambda.amazonaws.com
            Action: sts:AssumeRole
      ManagedPolicyArns:
        - !Sub 'arn:${AWS::Partition}:iam::aws:policy/service-role/AWSLambdaBasicExecutionRole'
      Policies:
        - PolicyName: TerminateChaosTargetInstance
          PolicyDocument:
            Version: '2012-10-17'
            Statement:
              - Effect: Allow
                Action:
                  - ec2:TerminateInstances
                Resource: !Sub 'arn:${AWS::Partition}:ec2:${AWS::Region}:${AWS::AccountId}:instance/${ChaosInstance}'

  CheckHealthRole:
    Type: AWS::IAM::Role
    Properties:
      AssumeRolePolicyDocument:
        Version: '2012-10-17'
        Statement:
          - Effect: Allow
            Principal:
              Service: lambda.amazonaws.com
            Action: sts:AssumeRole
      ManagedPolicyArns:
        - !Sub 'arn:${AWS::Partition}:iam::aws:policy/service-role/AWSLambdaBasicExecutionRole'
      Policies:
        - PolicyName: CheckEcsHealthAndAlert
          PolicyDocument:
            Version: '2012-10-17'
            Statement:
              - Effect: Allow
                Action:
                  - ecs:DescribeServices
                Resource: !Sub 'arn:${AWS::Partition}:ecs:${AWS::Region}:${AWS::AccountId}:service/${EcsCluster}/*'
              - Effect: Allow
                Action:
                  - sns:Publish
                Resource: !Ref ChaosTopic
              - Effect: Allow
                Action:
                  - kms:Decrypt
                  - kms:GenerateDataKey
                Resource: !GetAtt SnsKey.Arn

  ############################################################################
  # Lambda function 1: terminate the target EC2 instance
  ############################################################################
  TerminateInstanceFunction:
    Type: AWS::Lambda::Function
    Properties:
      FunctionName: chaos-terminate-instance
      Description: Terminates the target EC2 instance as part of the chaos experiment
      Runtime: python3.12
      Handler: index.handler
      Role: !GetAtt TerminateInstanceRole.Arn
      Timeout: 60
      MemorySize: 128
      Code:
        ZipFile: |
          import boto3

          def handler(event, context):
              """Terminate the EC2 instance supplied in the state machine input."""
              ec2 = boto3.client('ec2')
              instance_id = event['InstanceId']
              ec2.terminate_instances(InstanceIds=[instance_id])
              return {
                  'instanceId': instance_id,
                  'status': 'termination-initiated'
              }

  ############################################################################
  # Lambda function 2: check ECS service health and publish an SNS alert
  ############################################################################
  CheckHealthFunction:
    Type: AWS::Lambda::Function
    Properties:
      FunctionName: chaos-check-ecs-health
      Description: Checks ECS service health and publishes an SNS alert when unhealthy
      Runtime: python3.12
      Handler: index.handler
      Role: !GetAtt CheckHealthRole.Arn
      Timeout: 60
      MemorySize: 128
      Code:
        ZipFile: |
          import json
          import boto3

          def handler(event, context):
              """Check the health of an ECS service and alert on the SNS topic."""
              ecs = boto3.client('ecs')
              sns = boto3.client('sns')

              cluster = event['Cluster']
              service = event['Service']
              topic_arn = event['TopicArn']

              response = ecs.describe_services(cluster=cluster, services=[service])
              services = response.get('services', [])

              healthy = False
              details = {}
              if services:
                  svc = services[0]
                  desired = svc.get('desiredCount', 0)
                  running = svc.get('runningCount', 0)
                  pending = svc.get('pendingCount', 0)
                  status = svc.get('status', 'UNKNOWN')
                  healthy = status == 'ACTIVE' and desired > 0 and running >= desired
                  details = {
                      'status': status,
                      'desiredCount': desired,
                      'runningCount': running,
                      'pendingCount': pending
                  }

              result = {
                  'healthy': healthy,
                  'cluster': cluster,
                  'service': service,
                  'details': details
              }

              if not healthy:
                  message = 'ECS service health check FAILED. Details: ' + json.dumps(result)
                  sns.publish(
                      TopicArn=topic_arn,
                      Subject='ECS Service Unhealthy Alert',
                      Message=message
                  )
                  result['alertPublished'] = True
              else:
                  result['alertPublished'] = False

              return result

  # Step Functions state machine orchestrating the chaos experiment
  ############################################################################

    Type: AWS::IAM::Role

            Principal:
              Service: states.amazonaws.com
            Action: sts:AssumeRole

        - PolicyName: InvokeChaosLambdas
          PolicyDocument:
            Version: '2012-10-17'
            Statement:

                Action:

    Properties:
      StateMachineName: chaos-ecs-resilience
      StateMachineType: STANDARD
      RoleArn: !GetAtt StepFunctionsRole.Arn
      DefinitionString: !Sub |
        {
          "Comment": "Chaos experiment: terminate an EC2 instance, wait, then check ECS service health",
          "StartAt": "TerminateInstance",
          "States": {
            "TerminateInstance": {
              "Type": "Task",
              "Resource": "${TerminateInstanceFunction.Arn}",
              "Parameters": {
                "InstanceId": "${ChaosInstance}"
              },
              "Next": "Wait300Seconds"
            },
            "Wait300Seconds": {
              "Type": "Wait",
              "Seconds": 300,
              "Next": "CheckEcsHealthAndAlert"
            },
            "CheckEcsHealthAndAlert": {
              "Type": "Task",
              "Resource": "${CheckHealthFunction.Arn}",

        }

AWSTemplateFormatVersion: "2010-09-09"
Description: >
  Demonstrates creating SSM Parameters, a Secrets Manager secret with a
  dynamically generated password, and a Lambda function that retrieves and
  prints all parameters under the stack's path and all secrets matching that
  prefix using the SSM and Secrets Manager APIs.

Parameters:
  Environment:
    Type: String
    Default: dev
    AllowedValues:
      - dev
      - test
      - prod
    Description: Deployment environment used as part of the resource paths.

Resources:
  # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
  # IAM Role for the Lambda function
  # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
  LambdaExecutionRole:
    Type: AWS::IAM::Role
    Properties:
      AssumeRolePolicyDocument:
        Version: "2012-10-17"
        Statement:
          - Effect: Allow
            Principal:
              Service: lambda.amazonaws.com
            Action: sts:AssumeRole
      ManagedPolicyArns:
        - arn:aws:iam::aws:policy/service-role/AWSLambdaBasicExecutionRole
      Policies:
        - PolicyName: SSMParameterStoreAccess
          PolicyDocument:
            Version: "2012-10-17"
            Statement:
              - Effect: Allow
                Action:
                  - ssm:GetParameter
                  - ssm:GetParameters
                  - ssm:GetParametersByPath
                Resource:
                  - !Sub "arn:${AWS::Partition}:ssm:${AWS::Region}:${AWS::AccountId}:parameter/${Environment}/${AWS::StackName}/*"
              - Effect: Allow
                Action:
                  - ssm:DescribeParameters
                Resource: "*"
        - PolicyName: SecretsManagerAccess
          PolicyDocument:
            Version: "2012-10-17"
            Statement:
              - Effect: Allow
                Action:
                  - secretsmanager:ListSecrets
                Resource: "*"
              - Effect: Allow
                Action:
                  - secretsmanager:GetSecretValue
                  - secretsmanager:DescribeSecret
                Resource:
                  - !Ref DatabaseSecret
        - PolicyName: KMSDecryptAccess
          PolicyDocument:
            Version: "2012-10-17"
            Statement:
              - Effect: Allow
                Action:
                  - kms:Decrypt
                Resource: "*"

  # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
  # SSM Parameters under the stack's path
  # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
  ParameterOne:
    Type: AWS::SSM::Parameter
    Properties:
      Type: String
      Name: !Sub "/${Environment}/${AWS::StackName}/param-one"
      Value: "sample-value-one"
      Description: First sample parameter demonstrating SSM Parameter Store.

  ParameterTwo:
    Type: AWS::SSM::Parameter
    Properties:
      Type: String
      Name: !Sub "/${Environment}/${AWS::StackName}/param-two"
      Value: "sample-value-two"
      Description: Second sample parameter demonstrating SSM Parameter Store.

  ParameterThree:
    Type: AWS::SSM::Parameter
    Properties:
      Type: String
      Name: !Sub "/${Environment}/${AWS::StackName}/param-three"
      Value: "sample-value-three"
      Description: Third sample parameter demonstrating SSM Parameter Store.

  # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
  # Secrets Manager secret with a dynamically generated password
  # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
  DatabaseSecret:
    Type: AWS::SecretsManager::Secret
    Properties:
      Name: !Sub "${Environment}/${AWS::StackName}/db-password"
      Description: >
        Database password secret with a dynamically generated password. Created
        for the ParameterStoreDemo stack to demonstrate Secret retrieval.
      GenerateSecretString:
        SecretStringTemplate: '{"username": "appuser"}'
        GenerateStringKey: "password"
        PasswordLength: 32
        ExcludePunctuation: false
        ExcludeUppercase: false
        ExcludeLowercase: false
        ExcludeNumbers: false
        RequireEachIncludedType: true

  # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
  # Lambda function that prints parameters and secrets
  # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
  ParameterStoreDemo:
    Type: AWS::Lambda::Function
    Properties:
      FunctionName: ParameterStoreDemo
      Handler: index.lambda_handler
      Runtime: python3.12
      Role: !GetAtt LambdaExecutionRole.Arn
      Timeout: 30
      MemorySize: 128
      Environment:
        Variables:
          STACK_NAME: !Ref "AWS::StackName"
          SSM_PARAMETER_PATH: !Sub "/${Environment}/${AWS::StackName}"
          SECRETS_PREFIX: !Sub "${Environment}/${AWS::StackName}"
      Code:
        ZipFile: |
          import json
          import os

          import boto3

          ssm = boto3.client("ssm")
          secrets = boto3.client("secretsmanager")


          def lambda_handler(event, context):
              stack_name = os.environ.get("STACK_NAME", "")
              parameter_path = os.environ.get("SSM_PARAMETER_PATH", "")
              secrets_prefix = os.environ.get("SECRETS_PREFIX", "")
              region = ssm.meta.region_name

              result = {
                  "stack_name": stack_name,
                  "region": region,
                  "parameters": [],
                  "secrets": [],
              }

              # Retrieve all parameters found under the stack's path.
              params = []
              paginator = ssm.get_paginator("get_parameters_by_path")
              page_iterator = paginator.paginate(
                  Path=parameter_path, Recursive=True, WithDecryption=True
              )
              for page in page_iterator:
                  for param in page.get("Parameters", []):
                      params.append(
                          {
                              "name": param.get("Name"),
                              "type": param.get("Type"),
                              "value": param.get("Value"),
                          }
                      )
              result["parameters"] = params

              # Retrieve all secrets whose name starts with the stack's prefix.
              secret_list = []
              next_token = None
              while True:
                  kwargs = {
                      "Filters": [
                          {
                              "Key": "name",
                              "Values": [secrets_prefix],
                          }
                      ]
                  }
                  if next_token:
                      kwargs["NextToken"] = next_token
                  response = secrets.list_secrets(**kwargs)
                  for secret_entry in response.get("SecretList", []):
                      name = secret_entry.get("Name", "")
                      secret_list.append(name)
                      # Append the secret value for secrets matching the prefix.
                      if name.startswith(secrets_prefix):
                          try:
                              value = secrets.get_secret_value(SecretId=name)
                          except Exception as exc:  # pragma: no cover - defensive
                              secret_list.append(
                                  {"name": name, "error": str(exc)}
                              )
                              continue
                          secret_list.append(
                              {
                                  "name": name,
                                  "value": value.get("SecretString", ""),
                              }
                          )
                  next_token = response.get("NextToken")
                  if not next_token:
                      break
              result["secrets"] = secret_list

              # Print (log) the discovered resources.
              print("ParameterStoreDemo result: " + json.dumps(result, indent=2))
              return {
                  "statusCode": 200,
                  "body": json.dumps(result),
              }

Outputs:

    Description: Name of the ParameterStoreDemo Lambda function.
    Value: !Ref ParameterStoreDemo
  LambdaFunctionArn:
    Description: ARN of the ParameterStoreDemo Lambda function.
    Value: !GetAtt ParameterStoreDemo.Arn
  IAMRoleArn:
    Description: ARN of the IAM role used by the Lambda function.
    Value: !GetAtt LambdaExecutionRole.Arn
  DatabaseSecretArn:
    Description: ARN of the database password secret.
    Value: !Ref DatabaseSecret

    Properties:

      Name: "Custom-Inventory-Processes-Document"
      Content:
        schemaVersion: "2.2"
        description: >-
          Captures running database and caching processes on Linux and Windows
          instances into a custom inventory file.
        parameters:
          linuxProcessKeywords:
            type: String
            default: "CassandraDaemon,dse cassandra,mysql,postgres,redis-server,redis-sentinel,memcached"
            description: Comma-delimited Linux process keywords to search for.
          windowsProcessKeywords:
            type: String
            default: "sqlservr,cassandra,mysql,postgres,redis-server,redis-sentinel,memcached"
            description: Comma-delimited Windows process keywords to search for.
        mainSteps:
          - action: aws:runShellScript
            name: LinuxCustomInventory
            precondition:
              StringEquals:
                - platformType
                - Linux
            inputs:
              runCommand:
                - |
                  set -e
                  TOKEN=$(curl -s -X PUT "http://169.254.169.254/latest/api/token" -H "X-aws-ec2-metadata-token-ttl-seconds: 21600")
                  INSTANCE_ID=$(curl -s -H "X-aws-ec2-metadata-token: ${TOKEN}" http://169.254.169.254/latest/meta-data/instance-id)
                  INVENTORY_DIR="/var/lib/amazon/ssm/${INSTANCE_ID}/inventory/custom"
                  mkdir -p "${INVENTORY_DIR}"
                  IFS=',' read -ra KEYWORDS <<< "{{ linuxProcessKeywords }}"
                  RUNNING=""
                  for kw in "${KEYWORDS[@]}"; do
                    kw=$(echo "$kw" | sed 's/^[[:space:]]*//; s/[[:space:]]*$//')
                    if pgrep -f "$kw" > /dev/null 2>&1; then
                      RUNNING="${RUNNING}\"${kw}\","
                    fi
                  done
                  RUNNING="[${RUNNING%,}]"
                  TIMESTAMP=$(date -u +%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ)
                  printf '{"schemaVersion":"1.0","instanceId":"%s","timestamp":"%s","runningProcesses":%s}' "$INSTANCE_ID" "$TIMESTAMP" "$RUNNING" > "${INVENTORY_DIR}/Custom-Inventory-Processes.json"
          - action: aws:runPowerShellScript
            name: WindowsCustomInventory
            precondition:
              StringEquals:
                - platformType
                - Windows
            inputs:
              runCommand:
                - |
                  $token = (Invoke-RestMethod -Method Put -Uri "http://169.254.169.254/latest/api/token" -Headers @{ "X-aws-ec2-metadata-token-ttl-seconds" = "21600" })
                  $instanceId = Invoke-RestMethod -Uri "http://169.254.169.254/latest/meta-data/instance-id" -Headers @{ "X-aws-ec2-metadata-token" = $token }
                  $inventoryDir = "C:\ProgramData\Amazon\SSM\InstanceData\$instanceId\inventory\custom"
                  if (-not (Test-Path $inventoryDir)) { New-Item -ItemType Directory -Path $inventoryDir -Force | Out-Null }
                  $keywords = ("{{ windowsProcessKeywords }}" -split ",") | ForEach-Object { $_.Trim() }
                  $running = @()
                  foreach ($kw in $keywords) {
                    if (Get-Process -Name "*$kw*" -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue) {
                      $running += $kw
                    }
                  }
                  $timestamp = (Get-Date).ToUniversalTime().ToString("yyyy-MM-ddTHH:mm:ssZ")
                  $runningJson = (@($running) | ConvertTo-Json -Compress)
                  $content = '{"schemaVersion":"1.0","instanceId":"' + $instanceId + '","timestamp":"' + $timestamp + '","runningProcesses":' + $runningJson + '}'
                  Set-Content -Path "$inventoryDir\Custom-Inventory-Processes.json" -Value $content -Force

  CustomInventoryAssociation:
    Type: AWS::SSM::Association
    Properties:
      Name: !Ref CustomInventorySsmDocument
      AssociationName: "Custom-Inventory-Processes"
      ScheduleExpression: !Ref ScheduleExpression
      Targets:
        - Key: InstanceIds
          Values:
            - "*"
      Parameters:
        linuxProcessKeywords:
          - !Ref LinuxProcessKeywords
        windowsProcessKeywords:
          - !Ref WindowsProcessKeywords

Description: >-
  Creates an Amazon DataZone domain (with a configurable domain name defaulting
  to "cookbookChapter11"), two projects representing producer and consumer teams
  (SalesPublisher and MarketingConsumer), the IAM roles required for domain
  execution, data access (Glue, Redshift, and Secrets Manager permissions), and
  provisioning, plus an environment blueprint configuration that enables the
  DefaultDataWarehouse blueprint in the current region.

Parameters:
  DomainName:
    Type: String
    Default: cookbookChapter11
    Description: Name of the Amazon DataZone domain.
  DataWarehouseBlueprintIdentifier:
    Type: String
    Default: DefaultDataWarehouse
    Description: Identifier of the DefaultDataWarehouse environment blueprint to enable.
  DomainExecutionRoleName:
    Type: String
    Default: AmazonDataZoneExecutionRole
    Description: Name of the IAM role used for DataZone domain execution.
  DataAccessRoleName:
    Type: String
    Default: AmazonDataZoneDataAccessRole
    Description: Name of the IAM role used for data access (Glue, Redshift, Secrets Manager).
  ProvisioningRoleName:
    Type: String
    Default: AmazonDataZoneProvisioningRole
    Description: Name of the IAM role used for provisioning environments.

Resources:
  # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
  # IAM ROLES
  # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

  # Role assumed by DataZone and AWS Glue to execute the domain and its jobs.
  DataZoneDomainExecutionRole:
    Type: AWS::IAM::Role
    Properties:
      RoleName: !Ref DomainExecutionRoleName
      AssumeRolePolicyDocument:
        Version: "2012-10-17"
        Statement:
          - Effect: Allow
            Principal:
              Service:
                - datazone.amazonaws.com
                - glue.amazonaws.com
            Action: sts:AssumeRole
      ManagedPolicyArns:
        - arn:aws:iam::aws:policy/service-role/AWSGlueServiceRole
      Policies:
        - PolicyName: DataZoneDomainExecutionPolicy
          PolicyDocument:
            Version: "2012-10-17"
            Statement:
              - Effect: Allow
                Action:
                  - datazone:*
                  - iam:ListRoles
                  - iam:ListUsers
                  - iam:ListGroups
                  - iam:GetPolicy
                  - iam:GetRole
                  - iam:GetPolicyVersion
                  - iam:GetUser
                  - iam:ListPolicies
                  - ec2:DescribeRegions
                  - ec2:DescribeAvailabilityZones
                  - ec2:DescribeVpcs
                  - ec2:DescribeSubnets
                  - ec2:DescribeSecurityGroups
                  - ec2:DescribeKeyPairs
                  - ec2:DescribeNetworkInterfaces
                  - ec2:DescribeInstanceTypeOfferings
                  - sso:GetSharedSsoConfiguration
                Resource: "*"
              - Effect: Allow
                Action: iam:PassRole
                Resource: "*"
                Condition:
                  StringLike:
                    iam:PassedToService:
                      - datazone.amazonaws.com
                      - glue.amazonaws.com

  # Role used by DataZone project environments to access data in the lake
  # (AWS Glue), data warehouse (Amazon Redshift), and secrets (Secrets Manager).
  DataZoneDataAccessRole:
    Type: AWS::IAM::Role
    Properties:
      RoleName: !Ref DataAccessRoleName
      AssumeRolePolicyDocument:
        Version: "2012-10-17"
        Statement:

            Principal:
              Service:
                - datazone.amazonaws.com
                - glue.amazonaws.com
                - redshift.amazonaws.com
                - ec2.amazonaws.com
            Action: sts:AssumeRole
      Policies:

            Version: "2012-10-17"

              - Effect: Allow

                  - glue:GetCatalog

                  - glue:GetDatabases

                  - glue:GetTables
                  - glue:GetPartition
                  - glue:GetPartitions
                  - glue:BatchGetPartition

                  - glue:DeleteJob
                  - glue:StartJobRun

            Version: "2012-10-17"
            Statement:
              - Effect: Allow
                Action:
                  - secretsmanager:GetSecretValue
                  - secretsmanager:DescribeSecret
                  - secretsmanager:ListSecrets
                  - secretsmanager:ListSecretVersionIds
                  - secretsmanager:GetResourcePolicy
                  - secretsmanager:GetRandomPassword
                Resource: "*"
        - PolicyName: DataZoneDataAccessCommonPolicy
          PolicyDocument:
            Version: "2012-10-17"
            Statement:
              - Effect: Allow
                Action:
                  - s3:GetBucketLocation
                  - s3:GetObject
                  - s3:GetBucketAcl
                  - s3:GetObjectAcl
                  - s3:ListBucket
                  - s3:ListAllMyBuckets
                  - s3:PutObject
                Resource: "*"
              - Effect: Allow
                Action:
                  - ec2:DescribeAvailabilityZones
                  - ec2:DescribeVpcs
                  - ec2:DescribeSubnets
                  - ec2:DescribeSecurityGroups
                  - ec2:GetSecurityGroupsForVpc
                  - ec2:DescribeRouteTables
                  - ec2:DescribeNetworkInterfaces

                  - logs:DescribeLogGroups
                  - logs:DescribeLogStreams
                Resource: "*"

  # Role assumed by DataZone to provision and manage environment resources
  # (e.g., Glue/Redshift resources in the project environment).
  DataZoneProvisioningRole:
    Type: AWS::IAM::Role
    Properties:
      RoleName: !Ref ProvisioningRoleName

        Statement:
          - Effect: Allow
            Principal:
              Service:
                - datazone.amazonaws.com
            Action: sts:AssumeRole
      Policies:
        - PolicyName: DataZoneProvisioningPolicy
          PolicyDocument:
            Version: "2012-10-17"
            Statement:
              - Effect: Allow
                Action:
                  - cloudformation:CreateStack
                  - cloudformation:DeleteStack
                  - cloudformation:DescribeStacks
                  - cloudformation:DescribeStackEvents
                  - cloudformation:DescribeStackResources
                  - cloudformation:GetTemplate
                  - cloudformation:GetTemplateSummary
                  - cloudformation:UpdateStack
                  - cloudformation:ListStackResources
                  - cloudformation:ListStacks
                  - cloudformation:GetStackPolicy

                Action:

                  - glue:UpdateDatabase
                  - glue:DeleteDatabase
                  - glue:CreateTable
                  - glue:UpdateTable
                  - glue:DeleteTable
                  - glue:GetDatabase
                  - glue:GetDatabases
                  - glue:GetTable
                  - glue:GetTables
                Resource: "*"
              - Effect: Allow
                Action:
                  - secretsmanager:CreateSecret
                  - secretsmanager:GetSecretValue
                  - secretsmanager:DescribeSecret
                  - secretsmanager:UpdateSecret
                Resource: "*"
              - Effect: Allow
                Action:
                  - iam:GetRole
                  - iam:GetRolePolicy
                  - iam:PassRole
                Resource: "*"

  # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
  # AMAZON DATAZONE DOMAIN
  # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
  DataZoneDomain:
    Type: AWS::DataZone::Domain
    Properties:
      Name: !Ref DomainName
      DomainExecutionRole: !GetAtt DataZoneDomainExecutionRole.Arn
      Tags:
        - Key: Name
          Value: !Ref DomainName

  # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
  # DATAZONE PROJECTS (Producer / Consumer teams)
  # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
  SalesPublisherProject:
    Type: AWS::DataZone::Project
    Properties:
      DomainIdentifier: !Ref DataZoneDomain
      Name: SalesPublisher
      Description: >-
        Producer team project that owns and publishes data assets in the Amazon
        DataZone domain.

  MarketingConsumerProject:
    Type: AWS::DataZone::Project
    Properties:
      DomainIdentifier: !Ref DataZoneDomain
      Name: MarketingConsumer
      Description: >-
        Consumer team project that discovers and consumes data assets published

  # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
  # ENVIRONMENT BLUEPRINT CONFIGURATION (DefaultDataWarehouse)
  # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
  DefaultDataWarehouseBlueprintConfiguration:
    Type: AWS::DataZone::EnvironmentBlueprintConfiguration
    Properties:
      DomainIdentifier: !Ref DataZoneDomain
      EnvironmentBlueprintIdentifier: !Ref DataWarehouseBlueprintIdentifier
      ProvisioningRoleArn: !GetAtt DataZoneProvisioningRole.Arn
      EnabledRegions:
        - !Ref "AWS::Region"

    Description: Identifier of the created Amazon DataZone domain.
    Value: !Ref DataZoneDomain
  DataZoneDomainArn:

    Value: !GetAtt DataZoneDomain.Arn
  DataZoneDomainName:

    Description: ARN of the data access role.
    Value: !GetAtt DataZoneDataAccessRole.Arn

    Description: ARN of the provisioning role.
    Value: !GetAtt DataZoneProvisioningRole.Arn

Resources:
  # VPC required for the Cloud Map (Service Discovery) private DNS namespace

    Properties:
      CidrBlock: 10.0.0.0/16

      EnableDnsHostnames: true
      Tags:

    Properties:

  # AWS Cloud Map namespace (stack name with .local suffix)
  ColortellerNamespace:
    Type: AWS::ServiceDiscovery::PrivateDnsNamespace
    Properties:
      Name: !Sub "${AWS::StackName}.local"
      Vpc: !Ref Vpc

  # Virtual gateway: colorgateway
  ColorGateway:
    Type: AWS::AppMesh::VirtualGateway
    Properties:
      MeshName: !GetAtt Mesh.MeshName
      VirtualGatewayName: colorgateway
      Spec:
        Listeners:
          - PortMapping:
              Port: 9080
              Protocol: http
            HealthCheck:
              HealthyThreshold: 2
              IntervalMillis: 5000
              Path: /ping
              Protocol: http
              TimeoutMillis: 2000
              UnhealthyThreshold: 2

  # Virtual node: blue

    Type: AWS::AppMesh::VirtualNode
    Properties:
      MeshName: !GetAtt Mesh.MeshName
      VirtualNodeName: colorteller-blue-node
      Spec:
        Listeners:
          - PortMapping:
              Port: 9080
              Protocol: http
            HealthCheck:
              HealthyThreshold: 2
              IntervalMillis: 5000
              Path: /ping
              Protocol: http
              TimeoutMillis: 2000
              UnhealthyThreshold: 2
        ServiceDiscovery:
          AWSCloudMap:
            NamespaceName: !Sub "${AWS::StackName}.local"
            ServiceName: colorteller

  # Virtual node: green
  ColorTellerGreenNode:
    Type: AWS::AppMesh::VirtualNode
    Properties:
      MeshName: !GetAtt Mesh.MeshName
      VirtualNodeName: colorteller-green-node
      Spec:
        Listeners:
          - PortMapping:

              Protocol: http
            HealthCheck:
              HealthyThreshold: 2

              Path: /ping

              TimeoutMillis: 2000
              UnhealthyThreshold: 2
        ServiceDiscovery:
          AWSCloudMap:
            NamespaceName: !Sub "${AWS::StackName}.local"
            ServiceName: colorteller

  # Virtual router with 50/50 split route
  ColorTellerRouter:
    Type: AWS::AppMesh::VirtualRouter
    Properties:
      MeshName: !GetAtt Mesh.MeshName
      VirtualRouterName: colorteller-router
      Spec:
        Listeners:

    Properties:
      MeshName: !GetAtt Mesh.MeshName
      VirtualServiceName: colorteller
      Spec:
        Provider:

              - Effect: Allow
                Action:

  # IAM role that EventBridge assumes to start the automation, and through which
  # the automation execution is granted the automation execution role.
  # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

    Type: AWS::IAM::Role

        Version: "2012-10-17"
        Statement:
          - Effect: Allow
